design: Gate 0 v2 — frontal-face-present vs face-absent, single-source (confound-free)
rationale: Run 1 (Tears of Steel, faces vs scenes) was AMBIGUOUS because the face clips were groups/people-in-rooms, so a body region out-responded the face region, and it was a stylized off-distribution sci-fi short. v2 fixes this: FACE = one frontal face fills the frame; NONFACE = no dominant frontal face detected across the whole 10s window (people-with-backs/profiles/scenes). Both drawn from the SAME public-domain film (Charade, 1963, color live-action Hollywood — in-distribution for a Friends/CNeuroMod-trained model), both contain people, so the only systematic difference is a dominant frontal face. This isolates the face signal and controls for film, people/bodies, scene, and low-level statistics simultaneously. Clip starts were chosen from SUSTAINED runs (>=2 consecutive 5s samples of the same category) so each 10s clip is genuinely category-dominant, and spread >=45s apart for independence.

confirmatory_scene_source.name: McLintock! (1963)
confirmatory_scene_source.note: Clean people-free landscapes/interiors for a PPA place-selectivity positive control (reported, not gated).

notes: Objects/full 4-way (faces>objects AND faces>bodies) deferred: no free PD naturalistic film yields clean object + body + face + scene at n>=15 from one matched source; that upgrade needs a stock-video API key (Pexels/Pixabay) for modern single-face / single-body / object clips.
